## Welcome

Welcome to the Teslasuit API! This guide will help you take your first steps with the Teslasuit API — from setting up your environment to running your first haptic interaction.  
Make sure your Teslasuit is [connected](https://developer.teslasuit.io/blog/suit-tutorial-pairing-calibration/) to your PC or laptop before continuing.

## Requirements

To get started, make sure the following requirements are met:

- Teslasuit device connected and recognized by the system
- Teslasuit Control Center installed (for suit calibration)
- Teslasuit SDK added to your `PATH`. To add Teslasuit SDK to your `PATH`, please read [Environment setup](#environment-setup)

## Environment Setup

Before writing any code, make sure the Teslasuit SDK is available in your Python environment.  
If you're developing locally and the SDK is not in your `PATH`, you can use the following snippet to add it dynamically:
```python
try:
    import teslasuit_sdk
except ImportError:
    import os
    import sys
    sdk_path = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..'))
    sys.path.insert(0, sdk_path)
    import teslasuit_sdk
    print(f'Successfully added \'{sdk_path}\' into sys.path')
```

To install Teslasuit Python SDK as a Python library, follow the next instructions:

1) Open a terminal (with administrator rights on Windows)
2) Navigate to the folder with Python SDK, usually it's `C:\Program Files\Teslasuit\Studio\python_api\`
3) Check if the `README.md` file is present. Some Python packaging tools require this file for installation; if it's missing, create a new empty file named `README.md` in the folder.
4) Make sure you are in the folder containing the Python SDK (e.g., `C:\Program Files\Teslasuit\Studio\python_api\`) before running the next command.
5) Run the command `pip install .`

## First steps

### Connect the Suit
After connecting your Teslasuit to your PC or laptop, you're ready to explore its capabilities using Python.

To begin, you need to:

- Attach the device
- Initialize the API and Device
- Create a haptic playable

::: {.callout-warning}
⚠️ Safety: Please calibrate your suit in Control Center before using stimulation or haptic scripts. Start with conservative settings, confirm electrode placement, and monitor for any discomfort.
:::

### Run Your First Touch

Below is a complete example that demonstrates how to send a basic haptic touch to the right upper arm of the suit:

```python
import time
from teslasuit_sdk import ts_api
import teslasuit_sdk.subsystems.ts_haptic
from teslasuit_sdk.ts_mapper import TsBone2dIndex

# Touch parameters — adjust these to change the haptic sensation
TOUCH_FREQ_HZ     = 100                           # stimulation frequency in Hz (valid range: 1–150)
TOUCH_PERIOD_US   = 1000000 // TOUCH_FREQ_HZ    # period in µs; formula: 1000000 / frequency_hz
TOUCH_AMPLITUDE   = 40    # signal amplitude as a percentage (valid range: 1–100)
TOUCH_PULSE_WIDTH = 150   # electrical pulse width in microseconds
TOUCH_DURATION_MS = 1000  # how long the touch plays, in milliseconds

def main():
    print("Initialize API")
    api = ts_api.TsApi()  # create the central API object

    # Wait until the suit is connected, then get a reference to it
    device = api.get_device_manager().get_or_wait_last_device_attached()
    player = device.haptic  # haptic subsystem for creating and playing touches
    mapper = api.mapper     # mapper translates body-area names into channel lists

    print("Setup channels to play and touch parameters")
    # Build the full layout of haptic electric channels for this device version
    layout   = mapper.get_haptic_electric_channel_layout(device.get_mapping())
    bones    = mapper.get_layout_bones(layout)
    # Select only the channels that cover the right upper arm
    channels = mapper.get_bone_contents(bones[TsBone2dIndex.RightUpperArm.value])
    params   = player.create_touch_parameters(
        period=TOUCH_PERIOD_US,
        amplitude=TOUCH_AMPLITUDE,
        pulse_width=TOUCH_PULSE_WIDTH,
    )

    print("Create touch and play")
    playable_id = player.create_touch(params, channels, TOUCH_DURATION_MS)
    player.play_playable(playable_id)

    print("Wait until playback finished...")
    time.sleep(TOUCH_DURATION_MS / 1000)  # convert ms → seconds
    print("Finished")


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

## Test Your Setup

If the suit is connected and the SDK is installed correctly, running the script above should produce a short haptic effect on the right upper arm of the suit.

If nothing happens:

- Ensure the device is calibrated in the Control Center
- Check the connection
- Confirm that Python can import the teslasuit_sdk module
